Hi everyone! I'm Jacob Greenfield. I'm a PhD student studying electrical and computer engineering at Carnegie Mellon University, and I am interested in formal verification and systems programming languages (... and especially formally-verified systems programming languages!). Currently, I'm working on a mechanizing a correctness proof for a programming language for intermittent computing.

I've been learning and using Lean over the past few months. I just opened my first PR to Mathlib (https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/42995), adding a few small theorems to help with inserting an element into a list using orderedInsert in a way that preserves a certain preorder or other pairwise relation. This is helpful if multiple elements are sorted at the same "level", ie. when the relation isn't antisymmetric. Looking forward to learning more about Lean and the wonderful people who are building it. Thanks!
You might be interested in cslib then, perhaps even more than mathlib (you can search this Zulip for a the channel about it too)
